claim: The vacuole has a space-filling function, allowing particularly rapid plant cell expansion with very little increase in cytosolic content.
source: The vacuole has a space-filling function, allowing a particularly rapid plant cell expansion with very little increase in cytosolic content (Löfke et al., 2015; Scheuring et al., 2016; Dünser et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to three published studies (Löfke et al., 2015; Scheuring et al., 2016; Dünser et al., 2019).

claim: Very little is known about the mechanisms that define vacuolar size.
source: Despite its importance for cell size determination in plants, very little is known about the mechanisms that define vacuolar size.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field, based on the authors' assessment of existing literature.

claim: Cellular and vacuolar size expansions are coordinated.
source: Here, we show that the cellular and vacuolar size expansions are coordinated.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Endocytic membrane sorting from the plasma membrane to the vacuole is enhanced during rapid root cell expansion.
source: Our data reveal that endocytic membrane sorting from the plasma membrane to the vacuole is enhanced in the course of rapid root cell expansion.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5 and related analyses.

claim: Enhanced endocytic trafficking to the vacuole fuels vacuolar expansion and ensures coordinated augmentation of vacuolar occupancy in dynamically expanding plant cells.
source: While this 'compromise' mechanism may theoretically at first decelerate cell surface enlargements, it fuels vacuolar expansion and, thereby, ensures the coordinated augmentation of vacuolar occupancy in dynamically expanding plant cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and represents an inference about the biological significance of the findings.

claim: The vacuole occupies up to 90% of cellular volume in plant cells.
source: The vacuole, occupying up to 90% of a cellular volume, is the biggest organelle in plants and its size correlates with and determines the cell size (Owens and Poole, 1979; Berger et al., 1998; Löfke et al., 2015; Scheuring et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature (Owens and Poole, 1979; Berger et al., 1998; Löfke et al., 2015; Scheuring et al., 2016).

claim: Vacuolar size correlates with and determines cell size in plants.
source: The vacuole, occupying up to 90% of a cellular volume, is the biggest organelle in plants and its size correlates with and determines the cell size (Owens and Poole, 1979; Berger et al., 1998; Löfke et al., 2015; Scheuring et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature (Owens and Poole, 1979; Berger et al., 1998; Löfke et al., 2015; Scheuring et al., 2016).

claim: Vacuolar morphology is a reliable intracellular read-out for cellular expansion.
source: The size of the vacuole increases during cell expansion and vacuolar morphology is a reliable intracellular read-out for cellular expansion (Dünser et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Dünser et al., 2019.

claim: Dynamic regulation of vacuolar size allows plant cells to expand with little increase of the cytosol, maintaining a favorable cell surface to cytosol ratio during growth.
source: The dynamic regulation of vacuolar size allows plant cells to expand with little increase of the cytosol (Dünser et al., 2019), maintaining a favorable cell surface to cytosol ratio during growth.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Dünser et al., 2019 and represents an inference about the functional significance.

claim: The vacuolar SNARE complex consists of R-SNARE VAMP711, Qa-SNARE SYP22, Qb-SNARE VTI11, and Qc-SNAREs SYP51 and SYP52.
source: The vacuolar SNARE complex, consisting of R-SNARE VAMP711, Qa-SNARE SYP22, Qb-SNARE VTI11, as well as Qc-SNAREs SYP51 and SYP52, regulates hetero- and homotypic membrane fusion at the tonoplast (Fujiwara et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Fujiwara et al., 2014.

claim: The vacuolar SNARE complex regulates hetero- and homotypic membrane fusion at the tonoplast.
source: The vacuolar SNARE complex, consisting of R-SNARE VAMP711, Qa-SNARE SYP22, Qb-SNARE VTI11, as well as Qc-SNAREs SYP51 and SYP52, regulates hetero- and homotypic membrane fusion at the tonoplast (Fujiwara et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Fujiwara et al., 2014.

claim: Mutations in VTI11 lead to strongly affected, roundish, and partially fragmented vacuoles.
source: Mutations in the vacuolar SNARE subunit VTI11 leads to strongly affected, roundish, and partially fragmented vacuoles (Yano et al., 2003; Zheng et al., 2014; Löfke et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to three published studies (Yano et al., 2003; Zheng et al., 2014; Löfke et al., 2015).

claim: Root length of untreated vti11 mutants is hardly distinguishable from wild-type seedlings.
source: Despite the strongly affected vacuolar morphology, the root length, as well as the size of fully elongated epidermal cells of untreated vti11 mutants, were hardly distinguishable from wild-type seedlings (Figure 1A-D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1A-D.

claim: The size of fully elongated epidermal cells of untreated vti11 mutants is hardly distinguishable from wild-type seedlings.
source: Despite the strongly affected vacuolar morphology, the root length, as well as the size of fully elongated epidermal cells of untreated vti11 mutants, were hardly distinguishable from wild-type seedlings (Figure 1A-D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1A-D.

claim: Vacuolar occupancy of epidermal root cells in vti11 mutants is not distinguishable from wild-type.
source: Although vti11 mutant vacuoles are morphologically distinct from wild-type vacuoles (Yano et al., 2003; Zheng et al., 2014; Löfke et al., 2015), their vacuolar occupancy of epidermal root cells was not distinguishable from wild-type (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1F and citations to previous studies.

claim: Redundancy may ensure the space-filling function of the vti11 mutant vacuole and safeguard cell expansion.
source: This finding suggests that redundancy may ensure the space-filling function of the vti11 mutant vacuole and, thereby, likely safeguards cell expansion.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that vti11 mutants have normal vacuolar occupancy despite morphological defects.

claim: VTI11 and VTI12 can substitute for each other in their respective SNARE complexes.
source: VTI11 and VTI12 are able to substitute each other in their respective SNARE complexes with the vti11 vti12 double mutants being embryonic lethal (Surpin et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Surpin et al., 2003.

claim: The vti11 vti12 double mutants are embryonic lethal.
source: VTI11 and VTI12 are able to substitute each other in their respective SNARE complexes with the vti11 vti12 double mutants being embryonic lethal (Surpin et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Surpin et al., 2003.

claim: Twelve small molecules (VACs 1-12) were isolated that affected YFP-VAMP711 and vacuolar morphology.
source: Thereby, we isolated 12 small molecules (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) that affected YFP-VAMP711 and vacuolar morphology (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2), which we thus named vacuole affecting compounds (VACs) 1–12.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the small molecule screen, supported by data in Figure 2 and supplementary figures.

claim: VAC1 induced ectopic accumulation of vacuolar SNARE marker YFP-VAMP711 in aster-like structures adjacent to the main vacuole.
source: Here, we primarily report on VAC1 (N'-[(2,4-dibromo-5-hydroxyphenyl)methylidene]-2-phenylacetohydrazide), which affected vacuolar morphology (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) and induced ectopic accumulation of vacuolar SNARE marker YFP-VAMP711 in aster-like structures adjacent to the main vacuole (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: VAC1 precursors (2,4-dibromo-5-hydroxybenzaldehyde and phenylacetic acid hydrazide) did not cause alterations to vacuolar morphology.
source: VAC1 can be synthesized from 2,4-dibromo-5-hydroxybenzaldehyde and phenylacetic acid (PAA) hydrazide, but the application of these substances (here referred to as precursors) did not cause any alterations to vacuolar morphology (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A.

claim: PAA was not detected in VAC1-treated seedlings.
source: The ultra-high performance liquid chromatography-selected ion recording-mass spectrometry (UHPLC-SIR-MS) analysis however did not detect PAA in VAC1-treated seedlings (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B-D).
evidence: This is supported by UHPLC-SIR-MS data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3B-D.

claim: VAC1 is not detectably converted to PAA under the experimental conditions.
source: We conclude that VAC1 is not detectably converted to PAA under our conditions.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the UHPLC-SIR-MS analysis data.

claim: Three VAC1 metabolites (M1-M3) were detected in VAC1-treated samples.
source: On the other hand, in VAC1-treated samples, the UHPLC-UV-MS analysis revealed three additional peaks for potential VAC1 metabolites (M1-M3) with a retention time of 4.37, 5.26, and 5.39 min for M1, M2, and M3, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 3E-F).
evidence: This is supported by UHPLC-UV-MS data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3E-F.

claim: Metabolite M1 is the hydroxylated form of VAC1 (VAC1-OH).
source: Metabolite M1 was predicted to be the hydroxylated form (VAC-OH, Rt 4.37 min, [M-H-]: 424.9129 Da, calculated elemental composition C15H11Br2N2O3) and the other two derivatives relate to glycosylated forms.
evidence: This is based on high-resolution mass spectrometry analysis and exact mass determination.

claim: Metabolite M2 is VAC1-3-O-glucoside (VAC1-Glc).
source: The detected compound M2 likely represented VAC1-3-O-glucoside (VAC1-Glc, Rt 5.26 min, [M-H-]: 570.9706 Da, C21H21Br2N2O7) and M3 was identified as VAC1-3-O-6-O-acetylglucoside (VAC1-AcGlc, Rt 5.39 min, C23H23Br2N2O8, [M-H-]: 612.9805 Da) (Figure 2—figure supplement 3G).
evidence: This is based on high-resolution mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3G.

claim: Metabolite M3 is VAC1-3-O-6-O-acetylglucoside (VAC1-AcGlc).
source: The detected compound M2 likely represented VAC1-3-O-glucoside (VAC1-Glc, Rt 5.26 min, [M-H-]: 570.9706 Da, C21H21Br2N2O7) and M3 was identified as VAC1-3-O-6-O-acetylglucoside (VAC1-AcGlc, Rt 5.39 min, C23H23Br2N2O8, [M-H-]: 612.9805 Da) (Figure 2—figure supplement 3G).
evidence: This is based on high-resolution mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3G.

claim: VAC1-AcGlc is the most abundant VAC1 metabolite (56.3% ± 0.8%), followed by VAC1-Glc (31.3% ± 0.4%) and VAC1 (12.4% ± 0.6%).
source: Using UHPLC–UV (λmax = 291 nm for all compounds), we revealed VAC1-AcGlc (56.3% ± 0.8%) as the most abundant metabolite, followed by VAC1-Glc (31.3% ± 0.4%) and VAC1 (12.4% ± 0.6%), while the UV signal of hydroxylated VAC1-OH (<0.1%) was close to the detection limit of the photodiode array detector used (Figure 2—figure supplement 3H).
evidence: This is based on UHPLC-UV analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3H.

claim: A substantial amount of VAC1 undergoes glycosylation in planta.
source: This set of data shows that a substantial amount of VAC1 undergoes glycosylation in planta, which could affect its activity in long-term experiments.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the metabolite analysis data.

claim: VAC1A4 induced severe vacuolar morphology defects at 10 µM for 2.5 hr.
source: At the concentration and treatment time used for the subcellular effect of VAC1 (10 µM for 2.5 hr), solely VAC1A4, which displays an additional hydroxy group, induced severe vacuolar morphology defects (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4B.

claim: VAC1A4 shows some degree of toxicity as main root growth did not resume after wash-out.
source: While short-term (2.5 hr) VAC1A4-treated cells appeared viable (based on the intact extracellular propidium iodide [PI] staining) (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B), the main root growth did not resume after wash-out (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C), indicating some degree of toxicity.
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4B and 4C.

claim: The entity of VAC1 (phenyl and benzaldehyde rings) contributes to its effect on vacuolar morphology.
source: These results imply that the entity of VAC1 (phenyl- as well as the benzaldehyde rings) contributes to its effect on vacuolar morphology.
evidence: This is an inference based on structure-activity relationship studies with VAC1 analogues.

claim: VAC1 affects the distribution of vacuolar SNARE complex components YFP-VAMP711, pHGFP-VTI11, and SYP22-GFP.
source: When compared to YFP-VAMP711, we observed similar VAC1 effects on vacuolar morphology and strong aster-like protein accumulation of pUBQ10::pHGFP-VTI11- and pSYP22::SYP22-GFP- (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: VAC1 induced ectopic accumulation of vacuolar membrane marker VHA-a3-GFP.
source: VAC1 also induced similar ectopic accumulation of vacuolar membrane marker VHA-a3-GFP (Figure 2—figure supplement 5), suggesting that other tonoplast proteins are not excluded from the region of aster-like aggregations and that these structures are part of the tonoplast.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: VAC1-induced aster-like structures are part of the tonoplast.
source: VAC1 also induced similar ectopic accumulation of vacuolar membrane marker VHA-a3-GFP (Figure 2—figure supplement 5), suggesting that other tonoplast proteins are not excluded from the region of aster-like aggregations and that these structures are part of the tonoplast.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that tonoplast markers accumulate in these structures.

claim: VAC1 induced ectopic extensions of the vacuole.
source: When compared to control treatments, VAC1 induced ectopic extensions of the vacuole, which were reminiscent to the before mentioned aster-like structures (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: VAC1 induced clusters of vesicles in close proximity to the malformed vacuole.
source: In addition, we observed VAC1-dependent clusters of vesicles in close proximity to the malformed vacuole (Figure 2F), possibly visualizing defective vesicle delivery to the vacuole.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: VAC1 treatments prevent the fusion of FM4-64-positive endocytic vesicles to the central vacuole.
source: Strikingly, staining of the vacuolar membrane was absent in VAC1-treated samples and instead FM4-64 accumulated in roundish structures (VAC1 bodies) (Figure 3A). This set of data demonstrates that VAC1 treatments prevent the fusion of FM4-64-positive endocytic vesicles to the central vacuole.
evidence: This is supported by FM4-64 staining data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: VAC1 interferes with vesicle trafficking to the vacuole.
source: This finding corroborates our assumption that VAC1 interferes with vesicle trafficking to the vacuole.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that plasma membrane proteins accumulate in VAC1 bodies.

claim: VAC1 did not visibly affect clathrin light chain marker CLC-GFP and F-actin marker Lifeact-venus.
source: On the other hand, VAC1 did not visibly affect clathrin light chain marker CLC-GFP and F-actin marker Lifeact-venus (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Early and late endosome markers GOT1-YFP, VHA-a1-GFP, and RABF2A-YFP were not disrupted upon VAC1 administration.
source: Similarly, early and late endosome marker lines, such as GOT1-YFP (WAVE18Y), VHA-a1-GFP, and RABF2A-YFP (RHA1), were not disrupted upon VAC1 administration (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Early vesicle sorting toward the vacuole is likely not disturbed by VAC1, but stalls in close proximity to the vacuole.
source: This set of data suggests that early vesicle sorting toward the vacuole is likely not disturbed, but stalls in close proximity to the vacuole.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that early endosome markers are not affected by VAC1.

claim: BFA blocks endocytic trafficking toward the vacuole at the level of the trans-Golgi network (TGN).
source: To further assess VAC1-sensitive vesicle trafficking, we initially used brefeldin A (BFA), which is a specific inhibitor of ARF-GEFs (ADP-ribosylation factor – guanine-nucleotide exchange factors) and blocks endocytic trafficking toward the vacuole at the level of the trans-Golgi network (TGN) (Kleine-Vehn et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kleine-Vehn et al., 2008.

claim: VAC1-induced accumulation of SYP21-GFP in VAC1 bodies was significantly reduced in BFA co-treatments.
source: The VAC1-induced accumulation of vacuolar SNARE SYP21-GFP surrounded the FM4-64 accumulation in VAC1 bodies, which was significantly reduced in BFA co-treatments (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3E and F.

claim: VAC1 affects vacuolar vesicle trafficking downstream of the TGN.
source: We, hence, conclude that VAC1 affects vacuolar vesicle trafficking downstream of the TGN.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the BFA co-treatment experiments.

claim: Transcriptional repression of CORVET or HOPS inhibits root growth.
source: The transcriptional repression of CORVET or HOPS inhibits root growth (Figure 4A and B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A and B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: Seedlings germinated on VAC1 containing media displayed reduced main root growth.
source: In agreement, seedlings germinated on VAC1 containing media also displayed reduced main root growth (Figure 4A, B, F, G), suggesting that vesicle trafficking to the vacuole contributes to root growth.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A, B, F, G.

claim: Vesicle trafficking to the vacuole contributes to root growth.
source: In agreement, seedlings germinated on VAC1 containing media also displayed reduced main root growth (Figure 4A, B, F, G), suggesting that vesicle trafficking to the vacuole contributes to root growth.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that VAC1 reduces root growth.

claim: VPS39 depleted roots remained fully sensitive to VAC1.
source: Homotypic membrane fusion unlikely contributes to the VAC1 effect, because VPS39 depleted roots remained fully sensitive to VAC1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: Repression of CORVET function induced a partially resistant root growth to VAC1.
source: In contrast, the repression of CORVET function induced a partially resistant root growth to VAC1 (Figure 4A–C), suggesting that defects in heterotypic vesicle trafficking toward the vacuole contribute to the VAC1-dependent interference with root growth.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Defects in heterotypic vesicle trafficking toward the vacuole contribute to the VAC1-dependent interference with root growth.
source: In contrast, the repression of CORVET function induced a partially resistant root growth to VAC1 (Figure 4A–C), suggesting that defects in heterotypic vesicle trafficking toward the vacuole contribute to the VAC1-dependent interference with root growth.
evidence: This is an inference based on the CORVET repression experiments.

claim: Conditional knockdown of VPS3 had no visible effect on the distribution of YFP-VAMP711.
source: The conditional knockdown of VPS3 had no visible effect on the distribution of YFP-VAMP711 and the VPS3-deprived cells remained sensitive to VAC1-induced aberrations in VAMP711 localization (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: VPS3-deprived cells remained sensitive to VAC1-induced aberrations in VAMP711 localization.
source: The conditional knockdown of VPS3 had no visible effect on the distribution of YFP-VAMP711 and the VPS3-deprived cells remained sensitive to VAC1-induced aberrations in VAMP711 localization (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: VAC1 primarily interferes with vesicle fusion at the tonoplast downstream of heterotypic vesicle tethering complex.
source: We, accordingly, propose that VAC1 primarily interferes with vesicle fusion at the tonoplast downstream of heterotypic vesicle tethering complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the CORVET and HOPS experiments.

claim: VAC1-treated wild-type cells remarkably resembled the vacuolar morphology of untreated vti11 mutants.
source: In agreement, VAC1-treated wild-type cells remarkably resembled the vacuolar morphology of untreated vti11 mutants (Figure 4E) and, hence, we subsequently addressed the contribution of vacuolar SNARE VTI11 to the VAC1 effect.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: VAC1 attenuates root growth rates in a VTI11-dependent manner.
source: We concluded that VAC1 attenuates root growth rates in a VTI11-dependent manner, because when compared to wild-type seedlings the vti11 mutants were less sensitive to VAC1 (Figure 4E–H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4E-H.

claim: vti11 mutants were less sensitive to VAC1 compared to wild-type seedlings.
source: We concluded that VAC1 attenuates root growth rates in a VTI11-dependent manner, because when compared to wild-type seedlings the vti11 mutants were less sensitive to VAC1 (Figure 4E–H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4E-H.

claim: VAC1 interferes with the redundant, SNARE-dependent membrane delivery to the vacuole.
source: We accordingly conclude that VAC1 interferes with the redundant, SNARE-dependent membrane delivery to the vacuole.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the vti11 mutant experiments.

claim: VTI11 is not the sole or main target of VAC1.
source: Accordingly, we propose that VTI11 is not the sole or main target of VAC1, assuming functional redundancy at the level of vacuolar SNAREs and/or other accessory molecular targets.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that vti11 mutants still respond to VAC1.

claim: Elongating cells displayed higher BRI1-GFP and FM4-64 uptake into VAC1 bodies when compared to meristematic cells.
source: Elongating cells displayed higher BRI1-GFP and FM4-64 uptake into VAC1 bodies when compared to meristematic cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C, D and Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C, D and Figure 5A and B.

claim: BFA bodies showed greater FM4-64 signal accumulation in cells of the elongation zone when compared to cells of the meristem.
source: In line with the results from VAC1 treatments, BFA bodies also showed greater FM4-64 signal accumulation in cells of the elongation zone when compared to cells of the meristem (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: BFA and VAC1 visualize enhanced membrane sorting from the plasma membrane toward the vacuole during cellular elongation.
source: We, hence, propose that BFA and VAC1 visualize enhanced membrane sorting from the plasma membrane toward the vacuole during cellular elongation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the VAC1 and BFA experiments.

claim: Early and late meristematic cells displayed roughly a doubling of surface area and volume.
source: Hence, we next performed whole-cell 3D reconstructions of early as well as late meristematic cells and observed that these cells displayed roughly a doubling of surface area and volume (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This is supported by 3D reconstruction data shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: The volume of FM4-64 containing BFA bodies showed a much stronger relative size increase compared to cellular size increase.
source: Compared to the cellular size increase, the volume of FM4-64 containing BFA bodies showed a much stronger relative size increase (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This is supported by 3D reconstruction data shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: Endocytic membrane sorting toward the vacuole undergoes reprogramming in elongating cells.
source: We, hence, rather conclude that endocytic membrane sorting toward the vacuole undergoes reprogramming in elongating cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that BFA body volume increases more than cell volume.

claim: Co-localization between FM4-64 and YFP-VAMP711 at the vacuolar membrane was significantly lower in the meristematic zone when compared to the elongation zone.
source: Three hours after the relatively equal pulse staining of FM4-64 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B), the co-localization between FM4-64 and YFP-VAMP711 at the vacuolar membrane was significantly lower in the meristematic zone when compared to the elongation zone (Figure 5H, I).
evidence: This is supported by co-localization data shown in Figure 5H, I.

claim: Endocytic membrane sorting from the plasma membrane toward the vacuole undergoes significant rate changes during cellular elongation.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that endocytic membrane sorting from the plasma membrane toward the vacuole undergoes significant rate changes during cellular elongation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the co-localization experiments.

claim: The area increase of both cell and vacuole surface is remarkably similar during the course of cell expansion.
source: We found that the area increase of both cell and vacuole surface is remarkably similar during the course of cell expansion (Figure 6A left panel, B).
evidence: This is supported by 3D reconstruction data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: VAC1 induced a detectable imbalance of cell and tonoplast surface size within 2.5 hr.
source: To address this coordinative mechanism, we applied VAC1 and employed whole-cell 3D reconstructions (Figure 6A right panel). Within only 2.5 hr, VAC1 induced an already detectable imbalance of cell and tonoplast surface size (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by 3D reconstruction data shown in Figure 6A and C.

claim: Intensified membrane delivery is required at both the plasma membrane and the tonoplast during cellular expansion.
source: This result indicates that intensified membrane delivery is not only required at the plasma membrane, but similarly occurs at the tonoplast during cellular expansion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that VAC1 disrupts the balance between cell and vacuole surface.

claim: Membrane delivery greatly contributes to vacuolar size control.
source: Accordingly, not only actin- and myosin-dependent vacuolar unfolding (Scheuring et al., 2016), but also membrane delivery greatly contributes to vacuolar size control.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the VAC1 experiments and a citation to Scheuring et al., 2016.

claim: VAC1 induced slower root growth without delay.
source: VAC1 induced without a further delay a slower root growth (tip displacement) (Figure 6D and E), which correlated with reduced cellular expansion rates (Figure 6F and G) when compared to the solvent control.
evidence: This is supported by time-lapse data shown in Figure 6D and E.

claim: VAC1-induced slower root growth correlated with reduced cellular expansion rates.
source: VAC1 induced without a further delay a slower root growth (tip displacement) (Figure 6D and E), which correlated with reduced cellular expansion rates (Figure 6F and G) when compared to the solvent control.
evidence: This is supported by time-lapse data shown in Figure 6F and G.

claim: Vesicle trafficking to the vacuole is required for fast cellular expansion rates.
source: Accordingly, we conclude that vesicle trafficking to the vacuole is required for fast cellular expansion rates.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the time-lapse experiments showing that VAC1 reduces cellular expansion rates.

claim: Endocytic trafficking toward the vacuole coordinates cellular and vacuolar surface increase, enabling rapid cell enlargements in plants.
source: In summary, our set of data suggests that endocytic trafficking toward the vacuole coordinates cellular and vacuolar surface increase, enabling rapid cell enlargements in plants.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: The molecular target of VAC1 remains currently unknown.
source: Here, we isolated and characterized VAC1, which interferes with the final steps of membrane delivery to the tonoplast. The molecular target of VAC1 remains currently unknown, but the structure-activity assessment suggests that the entirety of the compound is contributing to its activity, possibly insulating a complex mode of VAC1 action.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge regarding VAC1's mechanism of action.

claim: VAC1 disrupts SNARE-dependent, heterotypic vesicle delivery to the tonoplast.
source: Our data suggest that VAC1 disrupts SNARE-dependent, heterotypic vesicle delivery to the tonoplast.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data from CORVET/HOPS and SNARE experiments.

claim: VAC1 may interfere with several subunits of the vacuolar SNARE complex or yet to be identified accessory proteins.
source: It is tempting to speculate that VAC1 interferes with possibly several subunits of the vacuolar SNARE complex or yet to be identified accessory proteins.
evidence: This is speculation about the potential mechanism of VAC1 action.

claim: Endocytic trafficking is accelerated at the onset of elongation.
source: Mechanistically, our data suggests that endocytic trafficking is accelerated at the onset of elongation, suggesting that plasma membrane-derived vesicles at least in part fuel the size increase of the vacuole.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing increased membrane trafficking in elongating cells.

claim: Plasma membrane-derived vesicles at least in part fuel the size increase of the vacuole.
source: Mechanistically, our data suggests that endocytic trafficking is accelerated at the onset of elongation, suggesting that plasma membrane-derived vesicles at least in part fuel the size increase of the vacuole.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that endocytic trafficking increases during elongation.

claim: Cell and vacuolar surface enlargements are coordinated.
source: We propose that cell and vacuolar surface enlargements are thereby coordinated and pinpoint the importance of vacuolar size control for cell expansion and overall root growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing similar increases in cell and vacuole surface area.

claim: The proposed reprogramming of membrane sorting occurs upstream or at the level of the TGN.
source: Not only VAC1 but also BFA treatments visualized higher rates of endocytic membrane accumulation in expanding cells. We, therefore, assume that the proposed reprogramming of membrane sorting occurs upstream or at the level of the TGN.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that both VAC1 and BFA show similar effects.

claim: The accelerated endocytic membrane flow toward the vacuole could relate to rate changes in endocytosis or shifts in endosomal sorting machinery.
source: The accelerated endocytic membrane flow toward the vacuole could relate to rate changes in endocytosis, but alternatively also the endosomal sorting machinery could shift the balance between endocytic recycling (back to the plasma membrane) and membrane drainage toward the vacuole.
evidence: This is speculation about the potential mechanisms underlying the observed changes in membrane trafficking.

claim: Enhanced delivery of plasma membrane-derived membranes toward the vacuole during cell expansion seems counterintuitive because it appears to slow down cell surface increase.
source: The enhanced delivery of plasma membrane-derived membranes toward the vacuole during cell expansion seems somewhat counterintuitive, because it appears to slow down the theoretically possible cell surface increase.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the apparent paradox of the findings.

claim: Draining membranes toward the vacuole may constrain crucial cell wall remodeling during cell expansion.
source: In addition, a high degree of membrane recycling at the plasma membrane is needed to fuel the high demand for cell wall synthesis (Robert et al., 2005; Ketelaar et al., 2008; Ebine and Ueda, 2015) and, hence, draining membranes toward the vacuole may even constrain the crucial cell wall remodeling during cell expansion.
evidence: This is an inference based on citations to studies about membrane recycling and cell wall synthesis (Robert et al., 2005; Ketelaar et al., 2008; Ebine and Ueda, 2015).

claim: The vesicle trafficking-based compromise model allows steady increase in vacuolar occupancy in dynamically expanding cells, enabling growth with little de novo synthesis of cytosolic components.
source: On the other hand, this vesicle trafficking-based compromise model for enlargements of plant cells allows the steady increase in vacuolar occupancy in dynamically expanding cells, which enables growth with little de novo synthesis of cytosolic components.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the functional significance of the findings.

claim: The coordinated membrane flow mechanism is able to synchronize cell and vacuolar surface increase, which is likely why plant cells excel in the speed of cellular expansion.
source: This coordinated membrane flow mechanism is able to synchronize cell and vacuolar surface increase, which is likely the reason why plant cells excel in the speed of cellular expansion.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the evolutionary/functional significance of the findings.
